How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: All three statements are correct, tracing India's exchange rate evolution from a pre-1991 basket-peg, through the 1991 devaluation, to a unified market-determined rate achieved by 1993 following the LERMS transition.

advanced.q: A country experiencing large, sustained capital inflows (FDI + FPI) far exceeding its current account deficit would most likely see its central bank:
o: Do nothing since the exchange rate will remain unaffected regardless of inflows
Face appreciation pressure on its currency, and may intervene by purchasing foreign currency (building reserves) to prevent excessive appreciation that could hurt export competitiveness
Automatically raise its fiscal deficit target
Immediately devalue the currency by law
advanced.e: Large capital inflows exceeding the CAD create excess dollar supply, exerting appreciation pressure; to protect export competitiveness under a managed float, the central bank (like the RBI) may intervene by buying foreign currency, simultaneously building up forex reserves.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Full current account convertibility means residents can freely convert rupees for permissible current transactions like trade payments, travel, and education expenses abroad without approval, subject to specified limits. 2. Partial capital account convertibility means some capital transactions (like certain categories of external borrowing or outward remittance under LRS) are permitted within defined limits, while others require approval or remain restricted. 3. India's rupee is fully and unconditionally convertible on both current and capital accounts for all resident and non-resident entities. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 correctly describe India's convertibility regime. Statement 3 is incorrect since capital account convertibility remains only partial, not full and unconditional, for residents and even for many non-resident transaction categories.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why India, despite running a persistent trade deficit in goods, has often had a relatively moderate overall current account deficit?
o: Because gold imports are banned in India
Because software/IT services exports and remittance inflows partly offset the merchandise trade deficit
Because India does not import any capital goods
Because the current account excludes services trade entirely
advanced.e: India's large invisibles surplus, driven by software/IT services exports and substantial remittance inflows from overseas workers, has historically offset a significant part of the merchandise trade deficit, moderating the overall CAD.

title: International Economic Organizations
desc: IMF, World Bank, WTO and other global bodies

basic.q: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) was established following which conference?
basic.e: The IMF was established at the Bretton Woods Conference, 1944, along with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank).

basic.q: The headquarters of the IMF is located in:
basic.e: The IMF is headquartered in Washington D.C., the same city as the World Bank.

basic.q: Which of the following is the founding institution of the World Bank Group, established in 1944?
o: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)
basic.e: The IBRD, established in 1944 alongside the IMF, is the original and oldest institution of the World Bank Group, lending mainly to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries.

basic.q: The International Development Association (IDA), part of the World Bank Group, was established in which year and mainly provides:
o: 1960; interest-free/low-interest loans and grants to the poorest countries
basic.e: IDA, established in 1960, provides concessional, interest-free (or very low interest) loans and grants to the world's poorest countries.

basic.q: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) primarily focuses on:
o: Promoting private sector investment and development in developing countries
basic.e: The IFC, established in 1956, is the World Bank Group's arm focused on financing and promoting private sector investment in developing countries.

basic.q: The Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) primarily provides:
o: Political risk insurance and credit enhancement to encourage foreign investment in developing countries
basic.e: MIGA, established in 1988, offers political risk insurance and guarantees to investors and lenders to encourage foreign direct investment into developing countries.

basic.q: The World Trade Organization (WTO) came into being on:
basic.e: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995, following the Uruguay Round of negotiations under GATT.

basic.q: The WTO is the successor organization to which earlier arrangement?
o: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)
basic.e: The WTO succeeded the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), which had governed international trade rules since 1947.

basic.q: The headquarters of the WTO is located in:
basic.e: The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

basic.q: The World Economic Forum (WEF), known for its annual meeting at Davos, was founded by:
basic.e: The WEF was founded in 1971 by Klaus Schwab, a German economist, and is a not-for-profit foundation, not an inter-governmental organisation.

basic.q: The New Development Bank (NDB), set up by the BRICS nations, was established following the summit held in which city?
basic.e: The New Development Bank was established via the agreement signed at the Fortaleza (Brazil) BRICS Summit, 2014.

basic.q: The headquarters of the New Development Bank (NDB) is located in:
basic.e: The NDB's headquarters is located in Shanghai, China.

basic.q: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) began its operations in which year?
basic.e: Though proposed by China in 2013, the AIIB formally commenced operations in January 2016.

basic.q: The headquarters of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is located in:
basic.e: The AIIB is headquartered in Beijing, China.

basic.q: Which institution primarily provides short/medium-term balance of payments assistance to member countries facing external payment difficulties?
basic.e: The IMF was created specifically to provide financial assistance to member countries facing balance of payments difficulties and to promote exchange rate stability.

basic.q: Which institution of the World Bank Group deals with settlement of investment disputes between states and foreign investors?
o: ICSID (International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes)
basic.e: ICSID, established in 1966, is the World Bank Group institution dedicated to arbitration and conciliation of investment disputes between states and foreign investors.

basic.q: The Uruguay Round of trade negotiations, which led to the creation of the WTO, was conducted under the auspices of:
basic.e: The Uruguay Round (1986-1994) was the eighth and final round of trade negotiations under GATT, culminating in the Marrakesh Agreement that established the WTO.

basic.q: India is a founding member of which of the following organizations?
o: Both the IMF and the World Bank
basic.e: India was among the original founding/signatory members of both the IMF and the World Bank at Bretton Woods in 1944.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The World Bank Group consists of five constituent institutions: IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, and ICSID. 2. All five institutions of the World Bank Group primarily lend directly to sovereign governments only. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Only statement 1 is correct. While IBRD and IDA lend mainly to governments, IFC finances private companies directly and MIGA provides guarantees to private investors, so not all institutions lend solely to sovereigns.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about the IMF: 1. Voting power in the IMF is based on a quota system linked to a member's relative size in the world economy. 2. The United States holds the largest quota and voting share in the IMF. 3. Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) are allocated to member countries in proportion to their IMF quota. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements are correct: IMF voting power is quota-based, the US holds the largest quota/vote share, and SDR allocations are made proportional to members' quotas.

intermediate.q: The IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development) primarily lends to:
o: Only the poorest, least creditworthy countries on a grant basis
Middle-income and creditworthy lower-income countries at near-market rates
Only member countries of the European Union
intermediate.e: Unlike IDA (which serves the poorest countries concessionally), the IBRD lends to middle-income and creditworthy poorer countries at market-based or near-market interest rates.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The WTO's dispute settlement mechanism allows member countries to challenge trade practices of other members before a panel. 2. WTO agreements cover trade in goods only and do not extend to trade in services or intellectual property. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The WTO does have a Dispute Settlement Body, but its coverage extends beyond goods to include services (GATS) and intellectual property (TRIPS) as well.

intermediate.q: The World Economic Forum (WEF) is best described as:
o: A treaty-based inter-governmental organisation of the United Nations
An independent, international, not-for-profit foundation that brings together political, business, and civil society leaders
A lending arm of the World Bank
intermediate.e: Unlike the IMF, World Bank, or WTO, the WEF is not a treaty-based inter-governmental body; it is a Swiss not-for-profit foundation known for its annual Davos meeting and reports like the Global Competitiveness Report.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements about the New Development Bank (NDB): 1. It was established exclusively by the BRICS countries. 2. Its first President was from India. 3. It focuses on financing infrastructure and sustainable development projects in BRICS and other emerging economies. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: All three statements are correct: the NDB was set up by the five BRICS nations, its inaugural President (K.V. Kamath) was from India, and its mandate centres on infrastructure and sustainable development financing.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best distinguishes the AIIB from the World Bank?
o: AIIB is a multilateral development bank focused primarily on infrastructure financing in Asia, initiated by China, whereas the World Bank has a broader global development mandate
AIIB has no other member countries besides Asian nations
AIIB and the World Bank are the same institution merged in 2016
intermediate.e: AIIB, though open to members beyond Asia, was conceived by China with a specific focus on financing infrastructure in Asia, whereas the World Bank has a much broader, longstanding global development mandate across sectors.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India is the largest shareholder in the AIIB after China. 2. India has also been one of the largest borrowers/beneficiaries of AIIB financing for infrastructure projects. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Both statements are correct. India holds the second-largest shareholding in AIIB after China and has also been among the largest recipients of AIIB project financing.

intermediate.q: The Marrakesh Agreement of 1994 is significant because it:
o: Established the WTO, concluding the Uruguay Round of GATT negotiations
Created the IMF and World Bank
intermediate.e: The Marrakesh Agreement, signed in April 1994, formally established the WTO, marking the conclusion of the Uruguay Round negotiations under GATT.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. GATT (1947) was a full-fledged international organisation with legal personality similar to the WTO. 2. The WTO, unlike GATT, has a permanent institutional structure and a binding dispute settlement mechanism. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Only statement 2 is correct. GATT was merely a multilateral agreement/treaty without a permanent institutional structure or full legal personality, unlike the WTO, which is a proper international organisation with binding dispute settlement.

intermediate.q: The 'Special Drawing Rights' basket of currencies used by the IMF currently includes which of the following, among others?
intermediate.e: The Chinese Yuan was added to the SDR basket in 2016, joining the US dollar, euro, Japanese yen, and British pound; the Indian Rupee is currently not part of the SDR basket.

intermediate.q: Which of the following best explains the primary purpose for which the IMF was originally created?
o: To provide long-term development loans for infrastructure projects
To promote international monetary cooperation, exchange rate stability, and provide temporary balance of payments support
To provide private equity to companies in developing countries
intermediate.e: The IMF was created to promote international monetary cooperation and exchange rate stability, and to provide temporary financial assistance to countries facing balance of payments problems, distinct from the World Bank's long-term development lending role.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The World Bank's IBRD raises most of its lending resources by borrowing in international capital markets, backed by its AAA credit rating. 2. IDA's resources come mainly from contributions by donor/wealthier member countries, replenished periodically. 3. IFC's resources are generated exclusively from UN budgetary allocations. How many of the above statements are correct?
intermediate.e: Statements 1 and 2 correctly describe how IBRD and IDA are funded. Statement 3 is incorrect; IFC raises funds mainly from capital markets and its own earnings/investments, not from any UN budgetary allocation.

intermediate.q: Which of the following statements about GATT is correct?
o: GATT dealt only with trade in services from its inception
GATT primarily dealt with trade in goods, and covered services and intellectual property only later, through subsequent negotiation rounds leading to the WTO
GATT never had multiple negotiating rounds
intermediate.e: GATT, established in 1947, focused mainly on trade in goods and tariff reduction; trade in services and intellectual property were brought under the multilateral trading system only through the Uruguay Round that created the WTO.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The AIIB was proposed by China in 2013 as an alternative/complementary institution to existing development banks. 2. Its founding membership was restricted only to Asian countries. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Only statement 1 is correct. While proposed by China, AIIB's membership was not restricted to Asian countries alone; it includes many non-regional members from Europe, Africa, and elsewhere.

intermediate.q: The Global Competitiveness Report and Global Gender Gap Report are flagship publications of which organisation?
intermediate.e: The World Economic Forum publishes influential reports like the Global Competitiveness Report and the Global Gender Gap Report, alongside hosting its annual Davos summit.

intermediate.q: Which of the following institutions is primarily concerned with providing insurance/guarantees against non-commercial (political) risks to attract foreign investment into developing countries?
intermediate.e: MIGA issues political risk insurance and credit enhancement guarantees, covering risks like expropriation, currency inconvertibility, and war/civil disturbance, to encourage FDI into developing countries.

intermediate.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Membership of the WTO requires a country to also be a member of the IMF. 2. WTO decisions are typically taken by consensus among member countries rather than by weighted voting as in the IMF. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
intermediate.e: Only statement 2 is correct. WTO decision-making is largely based on consensus among all members, unlike the IMF's quota-weighted voting system; WTO membership does not require IMF membership as a precondition.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The IMF's quota system determines both a member's voting power and its financial contribution/access to IMF resources. 2. Quota reviews are conducted periodically, and India's quota share has increased following the 2010 Quota and Governance Reforms. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both are correct. The IMF quota determines voting power, financial contribution, and access to resources, and periodic reviews (like the 2010 reforms, which took effect in 2016) have increased the voting share of emerging economies including India, China, and Brazil.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements about the World Bank Group's institutions: 1. IBRD lends to governments at near-market rates and requires sovereign guarantee. 2. IDA provides concessional finance to low-income countries based on income criteria and creditworthiness assessments. 3. IFC, unlike IBRD and IDA, can invest directly in private companies without requiring a government guarantee. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: All three statements correctly capture the differentiated roles: IBRD (sovereign-guaranteed, market-rate loans), IDA (concessional finance based on income/creditworthiness), and IFC (direct private-sector investment without sovereign guarantee).

advanced.q: Why is the World Economic Forum (WEF) NOT classified as an 'international economic organisation' in the same sense as the IMF, World Bank, or WTO?
o: Because it has fewer than 10 member countries
Because it is a private, not-for-profit foundation without a governing treaty among states, and its decisions/reports are not binding on any government
Because it does not deal with economic issues
advanced.e: Unlike the IMF, World Bank, and WTO, which are established by inter-governmental treaties with binding obligations on member states, the WEF is a private Swiss foundation that convenes stakeholders and publishes reports, without any binding authority over governments.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The WTO's predecessor, GATT, operated on a provisional basis for nearly five decades without formal ratification as a full international organisation. 2. The Uruguay Round, which created the WTO, also brought agriculture and textiles more fully within multilateral trade discipline. 3. The WTO's founding agreement explicitly excludes any dispute settlement role for the organisation, leaving disputes to be settled bilaterally. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; GATT indeed functioned provisionally for decades, and the Uruguay Round extended disciplines to agriculture and textiles. Statement 3 is incorrect since the WTO in fact established a robust, binding Dispute Settlement Body, one of its key institutional advances over GATT.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why emerging economies like the BRICS nations set up the New Development Bank (NDB) despite the existence of the World Bank?
o: To seek an alternative source of development finance perceived to have fewer political conditionalities and greater voice for emerging economies
Because the World Bank refused to lend to any BRICS country
Because the NDB is a subsidiary of the World Bank
Because the IMF mandated its creation
advanced.e: The NDB was conceived partly as an alternative to Bretton Woods institutions, driven by emerging economies' desire for development finance with greater voice/equal shareholding among founding members and comparatively fewer policy conditionalities.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. In the NDB, unlike the IMF and World Bank where voting shares are largely tied to capital contribution, the five founding BRICS members hold equal shareholding and voting power. 2. This equal-shareholding structure was a deliberate design choice to avoid dominance by any single member country. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both are correct. Unlike the IMF/World Bank's quota-based voting, the NDB's five founding members (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) each hold equal initial shareholding, a deliberate design to ensure balanced governance among founders.

advanced.q: A key criticism of the Bretton Woods institutions (IMF and World Bank) by developing countries has been that:
o: They have no lending programmes for developing countries at all
Voting power weighted by capital contribution/quota gives disproportionate influence to advanced economies like the US, despite reform efforts to rebalance shares
They are headquartered in Asia, far from major donor countries
They refuse to lend to any country in Asia
advanced.e: A long-standing critique is that the quota/capital-based voting structure of the IMF and World Bank gives advanced economies (especially the US, which holds effective veto power on major decisions) disproportionate influence relative to their share of the global population, despite periodic governance reforms.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The US holds a large enough voting share in the IMF to single-handedly block certain major decisions requiring an 85% supermajority. 2. India is among the founding members of the AIIB. 3. China holds the largest shareholding in the AIIB. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: All three statements are correct. The US's IMF voting share exceeds 15%, enough to block decisions needing an 85% majority; India is indeed a founding member of AIIB; and China holds the largest AIIB shareholding as its principal proposer.

advanced.q: The concept of 'conditionality' most closely associated with IMF lending refers to:
o: A requirement that borrowing countries implement specified economic policy reforms/adjustments in exchange for financial assistance
A rule that only democratic countries can borrow from the IMF
A cap on the number of loans a country can take
A requirement that all IMF loans be repaid in gold
advanced.e: IMF conditionality refers to policy commitments (like fiscal adjustment, monetary tightening, or structural reforms) that borrowing countries must undertake as a condition for receiving IMF financial assistance, aimed at correcting the underlying balance of payments problem.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The WTO's Agreement on Agriculture and Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) were both part of the package of agreements concluded under the Uruguay Round. 2. Prior to the WTO, intellectual property rights were not addressed at all in any multilateral trade framework. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Both the Agreement on Agriculture and TRIPS were indeed part of the Uruguay Round package; however, statement 2 overstates the case, as some intellectual property issues existed under earlier limited international conventions (like the Paris and Berne Conventions), even though comprehensive multilateral trade-linked IP rules came only with TRIPS.

advanced.q: Which of the following is the most accurate characterization of the relationship between the IMF and the World Bank?
o: They are the same organisation with different names used interchangeably

They are distinct sister institutions created at Bretton Woods, with the IMF focused on short/medium-term monetary and balance-of-payments stability, and the World Bank focused on long-term development financing and poverty reduction
The World Bank governs the IMF's operations
The IMF only lends to member countries of the World Bank
advanced.e: Though both born at Bretton Woods in 1944 and headquartered in Washington D.C., the IMF and World Bank are legally distinct institutions with different mandates: monetary/BoP stability versus long-term development financing respectively.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The AIIB's Articles of Agreement allow both regional (Asia-Pacific) and non-regional members to join. 2. The AIIB primarily finances infrastructure projects such as energy, transport, and urban development. 3. The AIIB operates entirely independently and has no co-financing arrangements with institutions like the World Bank or Asian Development Bank. How many of the above statements are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect; the AIIB has, in practice, engaged in several co-financing arrangements with institutions like the World Bank and Asian Development Bank for joint infrastructure projects.

advanced.q: Which of the following best explains why India, despite being a founding member of GATT in 1947, is sometimes described as having played a more assertive/prominent role after the formation of the WTO?
o: India became the WTO's headquarters host

The WTO's rules-based, binding dispute settlement system gave developing countries like India a more effective institutional platform to challenge trade practices of larger economies compared to GATT's weaker enforcement
India left GATT before WTO formation
WTO membership is different from GATT and India joined only in 2001
advanced.e: The WTO's binding Dispute Settlement Body, a marked improvement over GATT's weaker, consensus-blockable enforcement, gave developing countries including India a more credible mechanism to contest trade measures by larger economies.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Special Drawing Right (SDR) is a freely tradable currency that can be exchanged directly by private individuals in currency markets. 2. SDRs can be exchanged among member countries and the IMF for freely usable currencies, essentially functioning as a supplementary reserve asset among monetary authorities. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Only statement 2 is correct. SDRs are not directly tradable by private individuals; they function purely as a supplementary reserve asset that can be exchanged between central banks/monetary authorities and the IMF for actual currencies.

advanced.q: A country facing a severe balance of payments crisis is most likely to approach which institution first for emergency financial assistance tied to macroeconomic stabilisation conditions?
advanced.e: The IMF, unlike the WTO (trade rules body), WEF (forum/foundation), or MIGA (investment risk insurer), is specifically mandated to provide short/medium-term financial assistance to countries facing acute balance of payments difficulties, typically with attached policy conditionality.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements comparing the NDB and AIIB: 1. Both were established in the 2010s as multilateral development banks led by emerging/non-Western economies. 2. The NDB was set up jointly by five founding members with equal shareholding, while the AIIB has a shareholding structure weighted heavily toward its principal proposer, China. 3. Both institutions are entirely restricted to lending only within their founding member countries and cannot finance projects in non-member states. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Statements 1 and 2 correctly capture the establishment period and differing shareholding structures of NDB and AIIB. Statement 3 is incorrect since both institutions can, and do, finance eligible projects even in non-founding member countries that join later or qualify under their lending frameworks.

advanced.q: The term 'Bretton Woods System' historically referred to:
o: A system of floating exchange rates adopted after 1971
The post-World War II international monetary order based on fixed exchange rates pegged to the US dollar, which itself was convertible to gold, along with the creation of the IMF and World Bank
An early name for the WTO
A regional trade agreement in Europe
advanced.e: The Bretton Woods System, established in 1944, created a fixed exchange rate regime anchored to the US dollar (itself convertible to gold), alongside the founding of the IMF and World Bank; the system of fixed rates collapsed in the early 1970s, ushering in floating exchange rates.

advanced.q: Consider the following statements: 1. India was among the founding members of the WTO in 1995. 2. India had also been an original contracting party to GATT since 1947. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
advanced.e: Both statements are correct. India was one of the original contracting parties to GATT in 1947 and continued as a founding member when the WTO was established in 1995.
